item.title: The Houthis step up strikes on Saudi Arabia as the UN extends sanctions on Yemen
item.description:
Riyadh says it intercepted drones over its capital and Eastern Province on Thursday, while Yemen’s rebels claim attacks on oil and military sites. The Security Council has renewed sanctions on Yemen for another year.

On Thursday 12 November the spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, General Turki al-Maliki, announced the interception of drones over the Riyadh region and the Eastern Province, while the Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, claimed strikes on a pipeline, the port of Yanbu and two military sites, Al Jazeera reports. The attacks target the main route around Hormuz, with Riyadh saying it pumps some 4m barrels of crude a day through the East-West pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea, while Yemen’s government forces have pressed an offensive against the rebels since October. On Thursday the Security Council unanimously extended for a year the asset freezes and travel bans targeting Yemen and condemned the Houthis’ escalation, while Riyadh is urging the European Union to add them to its list of terrorist organisations, according to Reuters.

item.title: In Yemen, at least 30 killed at a market near Taiz, with each side blaming the other
item.description:
The Houthis accuse Saudi aircraft of bombing the Al-Hadara market on Friday; the recognised government blames Houthi missiles. According to the Yemen Data Project, October was the deadliest month for civilians since 2017.

At around 7am on Friday 6 November strikes hit the Al-Hadara market in the Al-Waziyah district of Taiz province, killing at least 30 people and wounding eight, according to the Houthi authorities, a toll the Associated Press could not verify. The Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, blames Saudi aircraft, while the spokesman for government forces, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, attributes the carnage to Houthi ballistic missiles and calls it a “war crime”. The attack is part of an escalation that began in July with the collapse of the UN-brokered truce, as the Houthis have besieged the city of Taiz for a month and the government’s “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, launched on 5 October, grinds on.
